title: Two Types of Lists
story: You're designing a student directory. One teammate says 'Use a Vec — just put everything in order!' Another says 'Use a Map — lookups will be instant!' Both have a point. But which one should you actually use? The answer is: it depends on what you're doing.
why: Choosing the right collection is a fundamental design decision — Vec for ordered iteration and sequencing, Map for keyed lookups and associations — and knowing when to use each prevents performance bugs and messy code.
analogy: Vec is like a numbered list on paper — find #3 instantly, but finding 'Bob' requires reading every line. Map is like a phone book with tabs — jump directly to the letter you need. Each tool excels at different jobs.
try_it: Measure which is faster conceptually: time how many loop iterations Vec takes vs Map's single operation. Add 50 students and search for the last one — Vec scans 50, Map checks 1. Then ask: when would you use Vec DESPITE it being slower for lookups? (Answer: when order matters — displaying a sorted list, pagination, or sequential processing.)
tips: Map lookup is O(1) — constant time regardless of size. Vec lookup by value is O(n) — grows with list size
If you need BOTH order AND fast lookups, consider maintaining a Vec for order and a Map for lookup simultaneously
For membership checks only (no values), use Set — it's optimized for just 'is this item here?'
common_mistakes: Using Vec for everything 'because it's simpler' — key-based lookups on large Vecs become painfully slow
Using Map when you need ordering — Map has no guaranteed iteration order; you'll need a separate Vec for ordering
Duplicating data without a plan — if you maintain both Vec and Map, keep them in sync or you'll get inconsistencies
